title: New Projects and Commissions
amount_raw: The maximum grant available in this category is £20;000.
eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations only; the organisation must have been operating as a non-profit for at least 12 months and must register on the Flexi-Grant portal at least one week before the deadline. Not open to individuals. Excluded project types: residency programmes, central or building costs, traditional memorials/figurative statues, commercial publishing, play equipment, community gardens and wellbeing activities; community projects only from non-profit arts organisations.
summary: Grants for exhibitions, exhibition catalogues and sculpture commissions that encourage new thinking about sculpture or sculpture history, or contribute to public awareness and appreciation of sculpture.
notes: Own page: 'Autumn — Applications now open — Submissions close 1 September, 23:00' on a 2026-08-14 snapshot, so status=open. LABELLING DECISION: the five Henry Moore Grants categories are recorded as FIVE rows rather than one, because each has its own eligibility class (organisations vs individuals) and its own stated maximum (£20,000 / £20,000 / £5,000 / £20,000 / £2,500) — the material facts a user needs differ per category, even though all five share one Flexi-Grant portal and one round calendar. FLAG FOR REVIEW: a reviewer may prefer a single 'Henry Moore Grants' row; if so, all five collapse. All four annual round closing dates are listed (multi_deadline). Year inference: the Autumn (1 September) and Winter (1 December) rounds carry no year on the page, but the Autumn round funds 'projects starting no sooner than 1 January 2027' and Spring/Summer are explicitly 2027, so Autumn/Winter are 2026. next_open_date is the Winter round opening (1 November, 9:00). amount_raw semicolon substitutes for the comma in the verbatim '£20,000'.

title: Acquisitions and Collections
amount_raw: The maximum grant available in this category is £20;000.
eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations only (12 months' non-profit operation; Flexi-Grant registration one week before the deadline). Not open to individuals. Same excluded project types as the other organisation categories.
summary: Grants to acquire new sculptural works for collections or to conserve sculpture in existing collections; cataloguing and display costs are also considered.
notes: Same round calendar and portal as the other Henry Moore Grants categories — see the notes on henry-moore-new-projects-and-commissions for the five-rows-vs-one decision and the year inference for the Autumn/Winter deadlines. Status open (Autumn round accepting until 1 September 2026).

title: Conferences, Lectures and Publications
amount_raw: The maximum grant awarded in this category is £5;000.
eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations only (12 months' non-profit operation; Flexi-Grant registration one week before the deadline). Not open to individuals. Commercial publishing projects are excluded, and exhibition catalogues must be applied for under New Projects and Commissions instead.
summary: Grants to publish a new book or journal or to stage a conference or other event related to sculpture.
notes: The lowest organisation-facing cap (£5,000), which is the main reason the categories are not collapsed into one row. Round calendar and portal as per henry-moore-new-projects-and-commissions.

title: Long-Term Research grants
amount_raw: The maximum grant available in this category is £20;000
eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations only (12 months' non-profit operation; Flexi-Grant registration one week before the deadline). Not open to individuals.
summary: Support for extended research projects requiring funding for more than one year, for example a permanent collection catalogue.
notes: Round calendar and portal as per henry-moore-new-projects-and-commissions. amount_raw is verbatim including the page's missing full stop; semicolon substitutes for the comma in '£20,000'.

title: Research and Travel grants
amount_raw: The maximum grant available in this category is £2;500.
eligibility_summary: The only category open to individuals: sculpture historians, academics and conservators researching and publishing on sculpture conservation, production, history and/or interpretation. Applications to inform or develop an artist's own work or professional practice are not accepted.
summary: Grants to individual researchers for research costs, travel, photography and archival access.
notes: The most directly researcher-facing Henry Moore opportunity and the only one open to individuals, so `restricted` is NOT tagged here (contrast the four organisation-only categories). Round calendar and portal as per henry-moore-new-projects-and-commissions. An example award is shown on the same page (a £3,000 research and travel grant to Amanda Geitner) which EXCEEDS the stated £2,500 maximum — noted as a page inconsistency, but the stated cap is used for amount_max_gbp.

title: Visiting research fellowships
amount_raw: UK – up to £600 / Europe – up to £700 / Rest of world – up to £1,000 (travel and subsistence), plus accommodation
eligibility_summary: Academics, curators and artists working on historic and contemporary sculpture who can make particular use of the Research Library, Archive of Sculptors' Papers and Leeds Sculpture Collections. Fellowships at Henry Moore Studios & Gardens (Hertfordshire) are restricted to projects relating to Henry Moore specifically. No studio facilities are available to artist fellows.
summary: A month (six weeks for Senior Fellowships) using the Foundation's research facilities in Leeds or Hertfordshire, with accommodation plus a travel and subsistence allowance. Three variants: Visiting Research Fellowships, Artist Research Fellowships and Senior Fellowships.
notes: Own page states twice: 'Applications are now closed for 2026/27 fellowship projects. The next round of fellowship applications will open in spring 2027' and 'We're not currently accepting applications for fellowships. You can apply on this page when our next round of submissions opens.' A stated future opening makes this forthcoming and therefore IN SCOPE, following the Leverhulme precedent that 'states a future open date' satisfies the inclusion rule; next_open_date is a season, not a date, so it is flagged. LABELLING DECISION: the three fellowship variants are ONE row, not three — unlike the grants categories they share a single application, a single round and a single expenses package, and differ only in duration and audience; the variants are named in the summary. FLAG FOR REVIEW if the reviewer prefers three rows. amount is an expenses allocation banded by the applicant's location, not a grant value, so amount_max_gbp (1000, the rest-of-world band) is flagged as an imperfect fit; accommodation is provided in kind and is unpriced.

title: Artist Award Scheme
amount_raw: fifty sculptors from across the UK each received a £2,000 grant
eligibility_summary: UK-based sculptors selected through a UK-wide nomination process involving leading voices from the non-profit arts sector. There is no application route.
summary: Unrestricted crisis-support grants to individual sculptors, run three times (2020: £60,000 to 40 artists; 2022 and 2025: £100,000 each round).
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: the page states in terms 'This is not a grant that can be applied for.' — it is not accepting applications and cannot be applied to at all. Recipients are nominated. No future round or opening date is given for a fourth round.
notes: A high-value distractor: a named, well-funded award scheme sitting on the grants page that an agent could easily report as an opportunity. £2,000 per artist is taken from the dedicated 2025 round page (site/henry-moore.org/what-we-do/grants-fellowships/artist-award-2025/index.html), which is a past-round page and NOT given its own row, per the treatment of round pages in the Leverhulme worked example. A press page (press/artist-award-scheme-2025/) and a press release about the 2022 £100,000 round are further distractors, also not rows.
